headline: Nothing concerning. The heart looks normal and there is no calcium in the coronary arteries (DIY Agatston score 0). Within what this scan covers, the lungs, vessels, bones and upper abdomen look healthy. Three small 'good to know' notes are listed below; none needs a follow-up scan.

impression.text: No coronary artery calcium: DIY Agatston score 0. Three independent AI adjudicators unanimously traced all 41 bright specks to low-dose noise and a table-step artifact. At 37, a zero is what most men have.
Normal heart: normal size (cardiothoracic ratio 0.39), no pericardial fluid, no calcium on the aortic or mitral valve, normal epicardial fat (≈76 mL) and normal left atrium (36-37 mm).

Ascending aorta 37-38 mm at its widest (36 mm at the radiologist's caliper level): upper end of normal for age, below the 40 mm 'dilated' line. No follow-up needed. It is a good baseline number for your doctor, especially if anyone in the family has had an aortic aneurysm or dissection.

One tiny (≈3 mm) solid micronodule in the left lower lobe, plus one or two even fainter specks that may be vessels seen end-on. Far below the 6 mm Fleischner threshold, so no follow-up is recommended for a low-risk person. Below the size the hospital's ClearRead AI reports.
Small Schmorl's nodes (disc imprints) in the T9 and T11 vertebrae, with borderline, sub-fracture (<20%) front-wedging of T9. Common and benign; only relevant if you have persistent mid-back pain.

Everything else checked is normal: pulmonary artery (≈26 mm; PA:aorta ≈0.7), descending aorta, lymph nodes (none enlarged), lungs and airways (no emphysema on the reliable reconstruction, no inflammation or scarring), pleura, esophagus (no hiatal hernia), liver (≈65 HU, no fatty liver), spleen, bone density (≈210 HU, healthy) and chest wall.

technique: Non-contrast, low-dose cardiac CT (Siemens SOMATOM X.ceed, 5 Nov 2026), 'calcium scoring only' protocol. Prospectively ECG-triggered sequential (step-and-shoot) acquisition in 4 table steps of ~34 mm, joined at z ≈ 1717, 1751 and 1785 mm. 120 kV-equivalent, 0.25 s rotation, CTDIvol 2.1 mGy, DLP 31.4 mGy·cm, effective dose ≈0.44-0.82 mSv (about 2-3 months of natural background). Heart rate 82-88 bpm; images reconstructed at 76% of the R-R interval (diastole). Reviewed reconstructions: calcium series (3 mm / 1.5 mm, Sa36d), axial soft tissue and lung (3 mm), thin lung (1.5 mm / 0.75 mm), 10 mm lung MIP, ClearRead vessel-suppressed, and coronal/sagittal soft-tissue reformats.
coverage: 13.8 cm of the chest, from about 8 mm above the carina down to about the T12 vertebra. Covered: the whole heart and pericardium, the ascending and descending aorta, the pulmonary arteries, roughly the lower 80% of the lungs, the mid/lower thoracic spine (≈T6-T11), ribs 4-11 partially, the liver dome, the top of the spleen and stomach. Not covered: the lung apices, aortic arch, upper mediastinum, thyroid, kidneys, adrenal glands and most of the abdomen, so nothing can be said about those.

systems.title: Heart & pericardium
systems.summary: Non-contrast, low-dose, ECG-triggered calcium-scoring CT. The heart is normal in size (axial cardiothoracic ratio 0.39), normally positioned (levocardia) and smoothly contoured. There is no pericardial effusion, thickening or calcification, and a normal, modest amount of epicardial fat (about 76 mL, mean -83 HU). No calcification is seen in the aortic valve/root, mitral annulus, myocardium or pericardium. There is no intramyocardial fat, LV apical aneurysm, fat- or calcium-containing intracardiac mass, or lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum. Blood-pool attenuation is normal (LV about 48 HU, ascending aorta about 55 HU), with no CT sign of anemia. LA AP diameter is 36-37 mm (normal). The only notable observation is a step-and-shoot banding artifact across the inferior heart (z about 1708-1730 mm, edge at z about 1717). It shifts attenuation by about ±20 HU and creates noise specks up to 170-200 HU in the inferior LV wall; it is not disease. Chamber volumes, wall thickness, RV:LV ratio, valve leaflets and coronary anatomy cannot be reliably judged without contrast.

checked.result: Normal: 0.39 at axial_st k=17 (z=1734.2), heart transverse 108.0 mm / inner thoracic 279.6 mm. Range 0.38-0.39 over k=15-18 (z 1728-1737); about 0.40 if the pericardial fat is included. Calipers visually verified (CTR_measurement_axial_st_k17.png). The AI 'heart' mask spills into the hilar pulmonary veins at z 1776 (spurious 115 mm width), so that level was excluded.
Not enlarged. AI whole-heart volume (myocardium + chambers) 430 mL; AI pericardial sac 572 mL. The heart is fully covered (z 1697-1813 within the 1682.5-1819 scan).

LV cavity 84 mL, RV 129 mL, LA 40 mL, RA 58 mL, LV myocardium 96 mL (about 100 g). These are approximate and not interpretable for chamber enlargement: the septum and endocardium are invisible, and the model draws a thick shape-prior myocardium band. Visually no chamber looks enlarged.

Normal: 36 mm (calcium k=50, z=1758.25) and 37 mm (calcium k=54, z=1764.25), measured along x=-15 from the posterior aortic-root wall to the posterior LA wall. The AI-mask maximum AP is 31.5 mm. Acquired at 76% R-R (mid-diastole), so the maximal end-systolic size may be slightly larger; still at most upper-normal.

Not directly measurable: the septum is isodense to blood, also on true short-axis reformats. The AI partition gives RV/(LV + LV myocardium) = 0.72, close to the roughly 0.7 expected for normal proportions; the AI cavity-only ratio of 1.54 reflects the thick-myocardium prior and is not interpretable. Indirect signs are normal: the LV forms the apex, the RA is not enlarged, IVC 19-21 mm (min) at the RA junction, main PA about 27 mm with PA:Ao < 1.

None. No water-density layer around the ventricles in any plane. An objective search for -10 to 30 HU pockets inside the sac found only: partial volume at heart-fat edges; unsegmented aortic-root and IVC blood; LV blood darkened by the banding artifact (z about 1710); and a roughly 10 mm mixed fat/vessel/trace-fluid triangle in the transverse sinus behind the aortic root (z 1773-1782, around (-10,-175), mean about 0-10 HU). That last one is normal (physiologic fluid and fat around the left main).

None. Where visible between epicardial and paracardial fat (e.g. calcium z 1713, x 30-40, y about -253), the pericardial line is below resolution: apparent FWHM 2.2-3.7 mm on 3 mm slices, and its peak never reaches soft-tissue HU (-40 to -2 HU). True thickness is ≤2 mm; no nodularity.
None (strict 100-300 HU 9 mm MIPs over the whole heart).

Normal and modest: about 76 mL (74-79 mL across axial_st/calcium/thin_lung) of fat (-190 to -30 HU) inside the AI pericardial sac, excluding the heart and great vessels. Mean -83 to -88 HU. Normal distribution in the AV grooves, interventricular grooves and over the RV (epicardial_fat_overlay_axial_st.png). With a 3 mm margin outside the sac (some paracardial fat): 102-107 mL.

checked.item: Myocardium: focal fat (old infarct, RV fatty infiltration)
checked.result: None. A search for fat-density voxels at least 3 mm deep inside the heart masks found only mask-boundary epicardial fat (LV lateral border, right AV groove, AIVG, inferior surface), each checked visually (intracardiac_fat_candidates.png).

checked.item: Myocardium: calcification / LV apical aneurysm / gross wall thickening
checked.result: No calcification. The LV apex and all contours are smooth on axial, coronal, sagittal and short-axis reformats, with no outpouching. Wall thickness cannot be assessed (myocardium isodense to blood); the AI myocardium volume of about 96 mL (≈100 g) does not suggest hypertrophy.
None (calcium series z about 1755-1775, calcium-window 6 mm and strict 100-300 HU 9 mm MIPs).

checked.item: Mitral annular calcification / other cardiac calcifications
checked.result: None. The posterior AV junction (z about 1730-1755) is clear. Outside the artifact band no voxel cluster in the heart reaches 130 HU on the calcium series; inside the band, peaks up to 174 HU are noise.

checked.item: Incidental coronary calcium (scored by a separate team)
checked.result: None convincing; agrees with the pipeline Agatston 0. The pipeline 'review' candidates #22/#30/#32 at (6.6,-165.7,1722.6), (-2.1,-167.9,1723.0) and (-2.4,-176.6,1724.2) lie in the inferior LV wall inside the banding-artifact slab. About 0.9% of LV voxels there exceed 130 HU (0% at z 1740), and peaks are 150-174 HU on the sharp calcium kernel with no discrete focus, so they are most consistent with noise (calcium_review_candidates_z1723.png).

checked.item: Blood-pool attenuation (anemia hint) and aortic ring sign
checked.result: Normal. Measured outside the artifact bands: LV 47-49 HU (r 6-10 mm at (22.1,-192.5,1739.5)), RV 46-51, LA 53-54, RA 48-52, ascending aorta 53-57 HU (r 10 mm at (-28.4,-197.8,1782.25)). The aortic wall is not denser than the lumen (no ring sign) and the septum is not visible, so there is no CT hint of anemia.

None. No fatty thickening of the septum itself. The largest fat in the interatrial region is 8.6 mm, in the posterior interatrial (Waterston) groove at (-17.5,-169.4,1734.2), which is extracardiac groove fat (threshold for lipomatous hypertrophy is 20 mm).
Small (about 3.4 mL by AI), normal triangular shape beside the pulmonary trunk (z 1770-1786), surrounded by thin fat, no calcification. Thrombus is not assessable without contrast.
No fat- or calcium-density mass. A soft-tissue mass would be isodense to blood and cannot be excluded on non-contrast CT.

Normal levocardia, apex to the left, normal contour. No signs of a pericardial defect (no lung interposed between the aorta and PA). Cardiophrenic angles show only normal fat pads, with no cyst or nodes. No sternotomy wires or devices. Heart rate during the scan was 82-88 bpm.
Not reliably traceable on low-dose non-contrast images, so not assessed (no gross abnormality seen in the fat around the aortic root).

findings.title: Step-and-shoot banding artifact across the inferior heart (not disease)
findings.description: A horizontal attenuation band crosses the inferior heart with a razor-straight edge at the table-step boundary z≈1716.6 mm (4 steps of about 34 mm over 136.5 mm; a subtler edge is at ≈1751). Directly above the edge (z≈1719-1730) the LV region measures about 65-70 HU versus 47-49 HU at z 1737-1740. Just below (z≈1711-1717) it drops to about 25-40 HU. On coronal and sagittal reformats the band edges are perfectly horizontal and run across chamber boundaries. The same z-step appears in non-cardiac tissue: right paraspinal muscle 41 to 82 HU across z 1716-1719, plus the spinal cord and descending aorta. So it is an acquisition artifact from the sequential (multi-heartbeat) scan at 85 bpm, not a myocardial or blood-pool abnormality. Practical consequences: (1) the dark band mimics 0-25 HU 'fluid' inside the LV at z≈1708-1716 in automated tissue maps; (2) the bright band produces scattered 130-203 HU noise clusters in the inferior LV wall at z 1719-1726. These include the calcium pipeline's three 'review' candidates near (6.6,-165.7,1722.6), (-2.1,-167.9,1723.0) and (-2.4,-176.6,1724.2), which I judge not to be convincing calcifications.
findings.plainEnglish: In a band near the bottom of the heart the picture looks artificially brighter, with a darker strip just below. That comes from the scanner stitching the image together from several heartbeats, not from anything in the heart, and it needs no follow-up. It also explains a few faint bright specks that look a bit like calcium but are not.
findings.location: Inferior heart (LV and inferior wall, also RV/RA), z ≈1708-1730 mm; step edge at z≈1717 (subtle second edge at ≈1751)
findings.recommendation: No action for the patient. For other readers and automated analyses: do not interpret HU or calcium candidates inside z≈1708-1730 mm without cross-checking another series or plane.

LV voxels ≥130 HU: 0.9% at z 1722-1724 vs 0% at z 1740; max in-heart peak 174 HU (calcium) / 203 HU (axial_st, 3 mm).

systems.title: Aorta & great vessels
systems.summary: This is a low-dose, non-contrast, ECG-triggered cardiac CT covering from about the carina to the upper abdomen (the aortic arch is above the field). The ascending aorta measures about 37-38 mm outer-to-outer at its widest, in the mid-ascending segment where the right pulmonary artery crosses. The double-oblique (true perpendicular) circle-equivalent is 38.0 mm; the overall range is 36-39 mm depending on method and edge threshold. This agrees with the radiologist's 36.1 mm caliper at axial_st k33, where my shortest chord is 36.2 mm and circle-equivalent 37.0-37.3 mm. That is high-normal for a 37-year-old man and below the conventional 40 mm 'dilated' threshold. The root and sinuses cannot be reliably measured without contrast. The descending aorta tapers normally from about 23.5 mm to about 18.6 mm. There is no aortic wall calcification and no sign of intramural hematoma. The main PA is about 26 mm perpendicular to its axis, the RPA about 20 mm and the LPA about 19 mm; the PA:aorta ratio is about 0.7, all normal. The SVC, azygos arch (about 5-8 mm), IVC and all four pulmonary veins look normal, and there is no persistent left SVC. One incidental ~3 mm calcified focus at the right paramediastinal/hilar border (lateral to the SVC) most likely represents an old calcified granuloma or lymph node and is benign.

checked.result: About 37-38 mm outer-to-outer, at the mid-ascending aorta (z 1785-1791, axial_st k34-36, centre LPS about (-28.8,-196.9)). His value matches the short axis at a level about 6 mm below the true maximum.

Clean periaortic fat with no stranding or fluid. Thin normal pericardial reflection/fat rim (about -30 HU, partial volume) around the ascending aorta, no fluid-density crescent.

findings.title: Ascending aorta high-normal size (about 37-38 mm), not dilated
findings.description: The ascending aorta measures 37-38 mm outer-to-outer at its widest point, at the mid-ascending level where the right PA crosses behind it. The double-oblique perpendicular circle-equivalent is 38.0 mm (ellipse 38.8 x 37.1) with the 0 HU edge, and 39.0 mm with the -25 HU edge. Axial, sagittal and coronal measurements on axial_st, calcium, thin_lung, sag_st and cor_st all fall within 36-39.5 mm. At the radiologist's level (axial_st k33) my short axis is 36.2 mm, matching his 36.1 mm caliper; the true maximum is about 1-2 mm larger and about 6 mm higher. The contour is smooth and round, with no calcification or wall abnormality. The root and sinuses cannot be reliably measured without contrast, and BSA indexing is not possible because height and weight are not available. In context: large non-contrast cardiac-CT reference cohorts (Framingham; Wolak et al. 2008) report mean ascending aortic diameters of about 32-34 mm in adult men. Upper limits of normal are roughly 38-41 mm overall and somewhat lower in men under about 45, because the aorta widens with age. So 36-38 mm is at the upper end of normal for a 37-year-old man (roughly the top 5-15%, depending on body size). It is below the common 40 mm cutoff for 'dilated' and far below the ≥45 mm aneurysm and ~50-55 mm intervention thresholds.
findings.plainEnglish: The main artery leaving your heart measures about 37-38 mm across at its widest, which matches the radiologist's 36 mm reading. That is at the upper end of normal for a man your age but below the 40 mm level where doctors start calling it enlarged, so it is not a problem in itself. It's a useful baseline number to share with your doctor, especially if anyone in your family has had an aortic aneurysm or dissection, or if you've been told you have a heart murmur or high blood pressure.
findings.location: Mid ascending aorta at the level of the right pulmonary artery crossing (z 1785-1791); radiologist's caliper slice z 1782.25
findings.recommendation: Guidelines do not call for imaging follow-up below 40 mm. Share the number with his doctor as a baseline and keep blood pressure well controlled. If there is a family history of aortic aneurysm or dissection or sudden unexplained death, a heart murmur, or Marfan-type features, a transthoracic echocardiogram would be reasonable: a bicuspid aortic valve is the most common cause of a large ascending aorta in young men, and an echo also measures the aortic root, which this scan cannot. Otherwise his doctor may choose to re-measure in several years.

votes.note:
I could not refute this finding. I measured it again with my own edge detector, not the reviewer's code. The detector takes the outer edge at the first drop from blood into fat, half-way between the two levels. Rays that run into a touching soft-tissue structure (MPA, SVC, RPA) are thrown out, and a robust ellipse is fitted to the rest. I ran it on three reconstructions (calcium Sa36d, axial_st Br40d, thin_lung Bl64d) and in two plane types (axial, and perpendicular to my own centerline). Every artifact check came back negative:
(1) Motion: the walls are crisp, with no double contour on the 0.31 mm calcium images. The posterior and left edges are 1.2-1.7 mm wide (10-90%), against 1.7-1.9 mm for the descending aorta.
(2) Pericardial-recess fluid or a wall rim: the edge-aligned mean profiles drop once, from about 50 HU straight to fat (-60 to -100 HU). There is no 0-30 HU shelf, so no fluid rim is being counted as wall.
(3) Table step: the technique reviewer puts join B3 at z about 1784.5, between the radiologist's level and the widest level. On zoomed sagittal and coronal views the walls run continuously across it. On the calcium series the circle-equivalent diameter rises smoothly: 35.6, 36.5, 37.3, 37.9, 38.2 and 38.3 mm at z 1776, 1779, 1782, 1785, 1787 and 1788. The widest stretch (z 1785-1797) lies entirely within one step.
(4) Oblique cut: the centerline is tilted only 5-9 degrees at the widest level, so axial and perpendicular results agree within 0.3 mm.
(5) Neighbouring structures: the fitted ellipses follow the visible outer wall at k32-k38 and do not include the PA, SVC or RPA.
(6) Geometry: the calcium series (512 px over 157.6 mm) and axial_st (695x512) agree within 0.3 mm.
If anything the aorta is slightly larger than the headline. Perpendicular to the centerline at z 1788 it measures 39.4 x 37.5 mm (circle-equivalent 38.4), about 0.4 mm above the reviewer's 0 HU result and in line with their -25 HU 39.0. A conventional 'maximum diameter' report would read about 3.9 cm, still under the 4.0 cm cutoff. I reproduced the radiologist's 36.1 mm at z 1782.25: my shortest chord there is 35.9 mm and the short axis 36.6 mm.
Context on interpretation: the descending aorta at the same level measures 22.1 x 21.0 mm, so the ascending-to-descending ratio is about 1.78. Reference cohort means are roughly 1.3-1.4 (from memory, not checked against the papers). The ascending aorta is therefore large relative to his own descending aorta. For a 37-year-old I would place about 38 mm near the 95th percentile (roughly the top 2-6%), which is a little more than the reviewer's 'top 5-15%'. That reads as 'upper limit of normal / borderline for age' rather than 'comfortably normal'. It is still not dilated by the usual 40 mm cutoff, and guidelines call for no imaging follow-up.
There is one sub-Agatston speck on the right-lateral wall: 0.57 mm2, maximum 147 HU, at z 1789.75, LPS (-44.5,-188.7). It is most likely noise, not calcification, so 'no wall calcification' stands.
Normal-variant with severity 1 is appropriate, though severity 2 is defensible because the recommendation is to tell his doctor. The echo suggestion is reasonable: it can look for a bicuspid valve and measure the aortic root, which this scan cannot.

I could not refute this finding. I re-measured it with my own code: first-descent edges at the local half-maximum, robust ellipse and circle fits, and visual QA of every slice used. I used my own centerline and three geometries (axial, double-oblique, and sagittal chords perpendicular to the vessel axis) on calcium, axial_st and sag_st. All agree that the ascending aorta is largest at the RPA level (z 1785-1791):
- 37.8-38.3 mm with half-max or 0 HU edges.
- 38.5-39.3 mm with generous edges (-25 HU, or half-max out to the lung).
- Double-oblique at z 1788.25: 38.8 x 37.4 mm, circle-equivalent 38.1; short axis about 37.4 mm.

At the radiologist's slice (axial_st k33, z 1782.25) I get a 36.6-37.0 mm short axis and 37.0-37.4 mm circle-equivalent. His 36.1 mm is within normal reader-to-reader variation (about ±2 mm), and his slice sits about 4-6 mm below the standard RPA level, where the vessel is about 1 mm wider. Above z 1795 the true perpendicular diameter tapers (36 mm at 1800, about 32-35 mm by 1806-1810). Axial and plain AP chords there read 39-40 mm, but only because the vessel tilts 10-33° backward into the arch.

**Measurement:** A physically unbiased edge probably gives about 38.5 mm. The reviewer's headline "37-38 mm" is slightly low, but they disclosed 39.0 mm for the -25 HU edge. No method reaches 40 mm.

**Criteria:** These are diastolic (76% R-R), non-contrast, outer-wall-to-outer-wall numbers, so the right comparison is the non-contrast cardiac-CT cohorts (Framingham, Wolak 2008, Mao 2008, Heinz Nixdorf Recall). Those report men's means of roughly 32-36 mm with an SD of about 3-4 mm, rising about 1 mm per decade. These cohort figures are recalled from memory and approximate. On that basis, about 38-38.5 mm puts a 37-year-old man of average size at roughly the 90th-96th percentile (top 5-10%). That is slightly narrower than the reviewer's "top 5-15%". If he is small (BSA under about 1.8 m²) it could be above the age- and size-specific upper limit. Height and weight are unknown, so it can't be indexed.

The aorta is below the 40 mm adult "dilated" convention and far below aneurysm and surgery thresholds, and no guideline surveillance applies under 40 mm. Severity 1 and the "high-normal / normal-variant" label are appropriate. I'd describe it as "borderline high-normal for age" rather than comfortably normal.

**Caveats for any future comparison:**
- A systolic-gated or ungated CT angiogram may read 1-3 mm larger in a young, compliant aorta; it could reach about 40 mm with no real growth.
- An echocardiogram (leading or inner edge) usually reads 2-4 mm smaller.
- Compare at the RPA level using the same method and cardiac phase.

**Other checks:**
- The root and sinuses can't be measured without contrast; I agree. Sagittal and coronal views show no disproportionate sinus bulge or tulip-bulb (Marfan-type) shape.
- The contour is smooth and round, with no motion-related double contour.
- Wall calcification: none meaningful. One equivocal sub-millimetre faint dot sits at the right-lateral outer wall at z 1788-1791, LPS about (-44.3, -188.6, 1789): peak 145-147 HU on calcium, 172 HU on axial_st, under 1 mm² above 130 HU, so not Agatston-scorable. The lumen control produced no blob above 130 HU. It is clinically irrelevant and is distinct from the reviewer's separate paracaval calcified focus about 10 mm away.

The recommendation is reasonable as written: share the number as a baseline, and consider an echo if there is a family history, a murmur or Marfan-type features, since an echo also measures the root and shows the valve.

NOT REFUTED; the measurement and the "not dilated" conclusion hold. I rebuilt everything from scratch with a different edge rule (local half-maximum, not fixed thresholds), my own centreline, and three series (calcium, thin_lung, axial_st). The maximum is at the mid-ascending aorta where the right PA crosses behind it, LPS about (-28.7, -197.3, 1789); axial_st k35 (z 1788.25) is the matching slice. Perpendicular outer-to-outer circle-equivalent there is 38.4-38.6 mm, with 37.8-38.2 at a 0 HU edge and 38.7-39.0 at -30 HU. The upper ascending aorta tapers to about 34-37 mm, so no larger segment is hidden toward the arch. The contour is smooth and round, with no wall calcium and no pericardial-recess fluid inflating the edge.

What a radiologist would report: an experienced reader would give the number and call it normal calibre (about 3.7-3.8 cm, perhaps "upper normal"), with no follow-up recommendation. Severity 1 and the guideline statement (no imaging surveillance below 40 mm) are proportionate. Neither alarmist nor dismissive.

One correction, on calibration: "top 5-15%" and "upper limits 38-41 mm" use all-age norms and are too reassuring for a 37-year-old. Framingham CT Table 2a (Rogers 2013) is the directly comparable reference: non-contrast, gated, axial at the right-PA level, outer-to-outer, mean of AP and transverse. For men under 45 it gives a mean of 30.3/31.1/33.2 mm and a 90th percentile of 34.2/34.5/37.0 mm for BSA <1.9 / 1.9-2.09 / ≥2.1 m². His Framingham-style value is about 37-38 mm, which is at or above the 90th percentile in every BSA stratum. That is roughly the 90th-95th percentile if he is a large man (his broad-chested habitus makes BSA ≥2.0-2.1 plausible) and roughly the 97th-99th if average-sized. Wolak's 41 mm upper limit (33 ± 4 mm) covers all ages. So "at or near the upper limit of normal for his age and size; not dilated by the adult 40 mm cutoff" is more accurate than "top 5-15%".

Recommendation tweak: mentioning it to his doctor at a routine visit is reasonable, so this is borderline between severity 1 and 2. A one-time baseline echocardiogram is a reasonable, low-cost, optional step even without red flags: this scan cannot assess the aortic root or the valve (bicuspid?). It is not urgent. The radiologist's 36.1 mm caliper at k33 is about 1.3 mm more conservative than the half-max outer diameter at that level (37.5-37.6); this is method variation, not a discrepancy.

findings.title: Tiny (~3 mm) calcified focus at right paramediastinal/hilar border, lateral to the SVC
findings.description: A well-defined, round, roughly 3 mm (2-4 mm) hyperdense focus sits at the right lateral mediastinal border, where the lung meets the mediastinum. It lies just lateral to and separate from the SVC (thin fat gap), in front of the right PA/right hilum, and abuts the medial right upper lobe. It is seen on axial_st k35-37 (peak 190 HU, mean about 150 HU in a 1.5 mm ROI, against blood at 58 ± 18 HU) and on calcium k71-72 (131-139 HU on the smooth Sa36d kernel). Because a small soft-tissue nodule next to lung would read lower, not higher, from partial volume, this indicates real calcification. The very high values on thin_lung (about 1000 HU) are not used, since that kernel's noise SD is about 257 HU. It is not part of the aortic or SVC wall. The most likely explanation is a calcified granuloma or a small calcified hilar lymph node (an old healed granulomatous infection); pericardial calcification is less likely.
findings.plainEnglish: There is a tiny speck of calcium, about 3 mm, next to the large vein on the right side of the chest. This is almost always an old, healed scar, such as a lymph node or small lung spot that calcified after a past and often unnoticed infection. It is harmless and needs no follow-up.

findings.title: One tiny (~3 mm) lung micronodule, plus one or two fainter specks
findings.description: Three tiny solid dots persisted after vessel suppression. The skeptic panel confirmed one as a definite micronodule: L0, left lower lobe lateral base, ≈3.0 x 2.2 mm (≈13 mm³), round, smooth, non-calcified, 12 mm from the pleura, isolated from vessels in 3D. A second (L7, LLL, ≈2.2 mm) is possible but faint. A third (L10, right upper lobe, ≈2 mm) more likely sits on a small vessel. Differential for L0: intrapulmonary lymph node or tiny granuloma.
findings.plainEnglish: There is one tiny round speck in the lower left lung, about 3 mm (the size of a pinhead), plus one or two even smaller, fainter dots that may just be blood vessels seen end-on. Standard guidelines (Fleischner 2017) recommend no follow-up scan for anything under 6 mm in a low-risk person.

votes.note:
I could not refute this finding. All three dots are real, repeatable densities and none is an artifact. The finding needs two corrections, and both point in the reassuring direction.

What I ruled out:
1. Noise: each dot is 14-23 SD above the surrounding lung. Each shows on 4-5 overlapping thin slices and on every reconstruction: thin_lung, 3 mm lung, 3 mm soft tissue, 10 mm MIP and CRVS.
2. Table-step artifact: the 4 sequential steps join at about z 1716.0, 1750.4 and 1784.9 (found from dips in slice-to-slice correlation). L0 and L10 are at least 10 mm from any join. L7 is 3.4 mm above the 1750.4 join, but it lies above the blended zone, and vessels crossing that join are smooth on coronal/sagittal, so the steps are not misregistered.
3. Vessel seen end-on: a true end-on vessel in this scan (LLL artery at LPS 18.4,-123.3,1771.8) looks just like the candidates on one axial slice. On coronal/sagittal it is a 5-8 mm tube, and CRVS removes it. L0 and L7 stay compact in 12 rotating-MIP directions and stay isolated in 3D down to a -650 HU threshold. The nearest vessel end to L7 is 7.7 mm away, with normal lung in between (the line profile drops to -830 HU).
4. Motion, streak or partial volume: the dots are 8-12 mm inside the pleura, away from the heart and diaphragm, and show no streaks or doubling.

Corrections:
(a) L10 is probably calcified, not "non-calcified". Its core reads 937-1828 HU on two thin slices (smoothed peak 603 HU). That is denser than every one of about 2,000 compact foci in the lungs of any size; for foci its size the 99th percentile is 324 HU. Local noise is not raised there. The most likely explanation is a tiny calcified granuloma (or calcified lymph node), which is even more clearly benign. It sits on a small RUL artery branch, about 4 mm from the minor fissure by the AI lobe masks. A vessel junction cannot be fully excluded from shape alone, but the density argues against a plain vessel. The 3 mm ST peaks cited as proof of "not calcified" cannot show this: all three dots fall exactly on the boundary between two 3 mm slices and are smaller than the slice, so each slice holds only about half of the dot.
(b) L7 is the weakest call. It is about 2 mm, low in contrast (below the median peak for vessels its size) and barely visible on the clinical 3 mm images. It is a real isolated focus that CRVS keeps, but a tiny nodule versus a short vessel piece is not certain.

Re-measured sizes (FWHM, which includes blur) are all at or under 3 mm, i.e. micronodules. Under Fleischner 2017 these need no routine follow-up, and nodules under 3 mm are usually not even measured. The CAD reporting 0 nodules is consistent with this, since they are likely below its reporting size. The clinical conclusion does not change: benign-looking micronodules, no follow-up, keep this scan as a baseline. Severity 1 (0 would also be defensible).

Not refuted. The sizes hold up and the criteria were applied correctly, but the claim of "three micronodules" is too strong. Only L0 is a definite micronodule. L7 is probable. L10 more likely sits on a small vessel than being a separate nodule.

L0 (LLL): CONFIRMED. A discrete, round, solid nodule about 3 mm across, not calcified.
- It stays isolated in 3D at every threshold from -650 to -350 HU, with no vessel running into it.
- It is by far the strongest leftover after vessel suppression: the top lung blob, at -10 HU smoothed, against -249 for the next.
- Its core density looks like ordinary soft tissue (rank 782 of 3437 lung maxima).
- It is 12.0 mm from the pleura (matches the reviewer) and 80 mm from the heart, so it is not a heart-motion artifact.
- Most likely an intrapulmonary lymph node or a tiny granuloma.

L7 (LLL): PROBABLE micronodule, about 2 mm. It is a compact blob in 3D, separate from nearby vessels. It is slightly elongated on the coronal view, so a short vessel segment cannot be excluded.

L10 (RUL): NOT convincingly a nodule.
- A small vessel runs through it in the axial plane (front to back) and obliquely on the sagittal view.
- At -650 HU it joins a vessel tree about 16 x 13 mm.
- On the 3 mm lung images it looks like a 4.7 x 1.4 mm linear density, which is how a vessel looks.
- The "starts and stops within 3-4 mm in z" test does not rule out a vessel lying in the axial plane.
- No fissure passes through it (the AI RUL/RML boundary is 4 mm away), so it is not a perifissural nodule.
- Its thin-slice core is the brightest in the lungs (mean of the top four voxels 1505 HU, next highest 1378), but that is within the noise tail of the vessels. Thin-slice soft tissue here has a noise SD of about 250 HU, and it shows no calcium density on the 3 mm soft-tissue window. So calcification can be neither shown nor excluded.
- Best read: a branch point or crossing on a vessel, or at most a tiny micronodule beside a vessel.

Criteria:
- Fleischner 2017 applies (incidental finding, age 37, which is 35 or over). For solid nodules under 6 mm or under 100 mm3, single or multiple: no routine follow-up at low risk, optional CT at 12 months at high risk. The reviewer stated this correctly.
- Under the Fleischner measurement guidance, spots under 3 mm (L7, L10) are called micronodules and are not measured. L0 averages 2.7 mm and rounds to 3 mm.
- The largest volume, about 13 mm3, is roughly 8 times below the volume threshold. The largest diameter is about half the 6 mm cutoff. Measurement error (about ±0.5 mm, ±2 mm3) cannot cross either threshold.
- Severity 1 (worth keeping as a baseline, no action) and the benign-incidental category are appropriate.

Partly confirmed, partly corrected. The clinical conclusion holds (tiny benign-appearing dots, no follow-up), but 'three micronodules' overcounts. L0 (LLL, LPS 113.7,-141.9,1726.8; thin_lung k59) is confirmed: a real, compact, round blob about 2.5-3 mm across, 12 mm from the costal pleura. It does not connect to any vessel in 3D, even at -600 or -650 HU, and it is the most blob-like isolated structure in either lung. It fits a tiny intrapulmonary lymph node or granuloma. L7 (LPS 105.5,-135.9,1753.8; thin_lung k95) is possible but weak: isolated and compact, but only about 2 mm and faint, near the noise and small-vessel floor. On the clinical 3 mm lung and 10 mm MIP series it cannot be told apart from small vessel dots. L10 (LPS -108.1,-229.0,1774.8; thin_lung k123) is refuted as a fissural non-calcified nodule. On the sagittal stack it is a bright spot on a continuous small vessel that runs from the anterior subpleural lung up and back to a branching vessel, with a Y-branch 1.5 mm above and a side branch 0.75 mm below. At -600 HU it joins a branching vessel tree (about 290-330 mm3, about 28 mm long). The so-called strand is a tube that branches and shows on only about 3 sagittal slices, so it is not the minor fissure (4 mm away by AI lobe labels). Its core is unusually dense on the sharp kernel (raw 1828 HU, the highest of 2069 similar lung maxima). So it is either a vessel junction plus noise or a tiny calcified focus. Either way it is not a reportable non-calcified nodule, and 'non-calcified' cannot be asserted at 2 mm on a 2.1 mGy scan. Clinical relevance: all three are 3 mm or smaller. By Fleischner measurement guidance (Bankier 2017), nodules under 3 mm are called micronodules and are not measured, so the 0.1 mm sizes and mm3 volumes are false precision. By Fleischner 2017 (applies at age 35 or older), solid nodules under 6 mm, single or multiple, need no routine follow-up in a low-risk patient, and at most an optional 12-month CT if high risk. Tiny nodules like these are common in adults. The ClearRead CAD flagged none. On the clinical series an experienced radiologist reading a calcium-score CT for a healthy 37-year-old would most likely leave them out or write one line, such as 'a few tiny (3 mm or smaller) micronodules, likely benign, no follow-up needed'. The recommendation (no follow-up; keep the exam as a baseline) is proportionate, neither alarmist nor dismissive. Severity lowered from 1 to 0 (nothing to do; 1 is acceptable at most). Suggested wording for the patient: one, maybe two, tiny 2-3 mm dots in the left lower lung, almost certainly a small lymph node or old scar, which are very common and need nothing. The third spot is most likely just a blood vessel.

findings.title: Sequential step-junction artifact at the diaphragm domes mimicking focal lucency
findings.description: On sagittal and coronal soft-kernel reformats, a perfectly straight horizontal dark band runs across both lung bases along the tops of the hemidiaphragms at z ~1716-1719 mm, and the dome tops look artificially flattened. RML LAA-950 is 20.7% within slices #9-15 versus 5.0% in all other RML slices. It has no wall and no lobular or segmental margin, vessels pass through it normally, and it follows the acquisition plane rather than anatomy. It is therefore an artifact, not emphysema, air trapping or a bulla.

findings.description: Raw LAA-950 is 42% on thin_lung (1.5 mm, Bl64d) and 37% on axial_lung (3 mm, Bl64d), values that would suggest severe emphysema. The sub-950 HU voxels, however, form a uniform salt-and-pepper speckle throughout visually normal lung. The cause is the very low dose combined with a sharp kernel (air noise SD ~88-157 HU), with the data floor-clipped at -1024 HU (48-87% of air voxels at the floor). Smoothing floor-clipped data biases low HU upward (smoothed air reads ~-960 HU), so the smoothed thin-lung values slightly underestimate; axial_st is the most trustworthy densitometry source.

findings.title: T9 inferior-endplate Schmorl's node with borderline (<20%) anterior wedging
findings.description: Corticated, dome-shaped central depression of the T9 (presumed) inferior endplate, ~9 mm transverse x 12 mm AP x 6 mm deep (apex z~1744.5), with a sclerotic rim and a ~3 mm dense ossific/calcific fleck at its anterior margin in the anterior annulus (z~1736.5-1738.8). votes.note:
I could not refute this. The T9 (presumed) inferior-endplate lesion is a real, old-looking Schmorl's node. It is not an artifact or a normal variant.

1. **Seen in every reconstruction.** It shows up in five separate reconstructions with the same 3D shape: sag_st #94-#99, cor_st #95-#98, axial_st #18-#20, thin_lung #74-#81 plus my own thin_lung sagittal/coronal reformats, and the calcium series.
2. **Its shape.** It is one central, steep-walled, tented dip in the endplate that opens into the T9-10 disc. The apex is at about LPS (-15.5, -113.5, 1743-1744.5).
3. **Contents and rim.** On axial_st #19 it is a ring with a sclerotic (dense) rim, and its contents measure about 95 HU, which is disc-like. That rules out fat and gas.

**Artifact checks:**
- **Table-step seams.** I estimated the seams at about z 1716, 1750.5 and 1785, from periodic dips in image noise and a visible line near 1717. The node lies entirely within one step (1716-1750.5). It also shows on in-plane axial images, which a step artifact cannot produce.
- **No misregistration at the seam.** The 1750.5 seam passes through the T9 body, but the front and back cortex edges move by 0.5 mm or less across it.
- **Normal variants ruled out.**
  - It is not a vessel seen end-on: it is corticated, connects to the disc, and is away from the basivertebral foramen.
  - It is not a Cupid's bow: it is single, central and thoracic.
  - It is not the normal shallow central dip of the endplate: it is 5-6 mm deep with a sclerotic ring.
- **Nothing acute.** The T10 superior endplate opposite it is smooth. The disc is no narrower than at T8-9. There is no soft-tissue swelling beside the spine. So there are no signs of disc infection (discitis) or an acute fracture.

**Anterior fleck:** this is also real. It appears in all five series at peak 700-1200 HU, centred at about (-14, -121.5, 1735.5-1739). It sits about 6 mm behind the front cortex, at the front lip of the node, and hangs 1-2 mm into the disc. This fits a small bony or calcified fragment at the mouth of the node, and it is benign. "Inner anterior annulus / node lip" describes its position more accurately than "anterior annulus".

**Wedging:** I reproduced the reviewer's numbers independently, and they are not caused by the seam. T9 front/back height ratio is 0.81-0.84, against 0.90-0.93 at T8 and about 1.0 at T10. An 18% front-to-back difference at a mid-thoracic level is within the normal range of physiological wedging. It is below the Genant grade 1 threshold, so it is grade 0. I would call it mild physiologic or developmental wedging rather than a "borderline" deformity. The middle height is lower only because of the node itself.

**Level:** the T9 label matches the TotalSegmentator labels. This limited scan has no T1 or L5 to count from, so the level is uncertain by one either way.

**Overall:** benign and incidental, no action needed. I would raise the confidence that the node is real from 0.8 to about 0.9 or higher.

Not refuted. I tried to disprove it and could not. Both the node and the wedging measurements hold up when I re-measure them myself.

1) The node is real and is not an artifact. It shows on the sagittal reformat (sag_st #95-98), the coronal reformat (cor_st #95-98), axial_st #19 (z=1740.25), and thin_lung #74-80, which is a separate reconstruction with a different kernel. It is a sharp, tent-shaped depression in the middle of the T9 lower endplate, with a dense (sclerotic) rim. The deepest point is at about LPS (-15.7, -113.7, 1742.5) on the inner surface, and the rim tops out near z=1744-1745. The table-step join is at z=1750.75, about 6 mm above it. The front and back walls of the vertebra run straight across that join; their edges shift by less than 0.3 mm, smoothly. My size is about 9.5 mm side to side × 9-10 mm front to back (where the dip is more than 0.5 mm deep) × 4.5-5 mm deep to the inner roof (about 6-7 mm to the top of the rim). The reviewer's 9×12×6 mm is slightly larger front to back and in depth. That is a difference in where the edges are drawn and changes nothing.

The fleck is confirmed: about 2-3 mm, at roughly LPS (-15, -122, 1737.8), z 1736.5-1739 (axial_st #18, thin_lung #74). It sits at the endplate/disc-rim junction, between the front corner and the node. The front-lower corner of T9 itself is intact at z≈1737.0, so the front height comes out the same whether or not the fleck is counted.

2) The front/back height ratio reproduces. I found the bone edges with my own half-max edge profiles at insets of 1.5-3 mm, across sag_st slices from x=-10.5 to -22.5, and checked them visually.
- T9: front height (Ha) 16.6-17.0 mm, back height (Hp) 20.4-20.5 mm, ratio 0.82 (range 0.81-0.84). A separate thin_lung resample gives 0.83.
- Neighbours: T8 19.9/21.9 = 0.90-0.91; T10 22.0-22.2/22.3-22.5 = 0.98-0.99 (reviewer said 0.95); T7 about 0.91.
- Wedge angle: the reviewer's 5.8° does not match their own ratio. A 3.7 mm difference over the roughly 23 mm between measuring lines gives about 8.5° measured corner to corner.

3) Applying the standard criteria:
- Genant method: front height is 16-19% lower than back height, which is under the 20% cut-off for a fracture. Grade 0, borderline at most.
- Normal values for this level: the usual T9 ratio is about 0.88-0.90 (SD about 0.05), so 0.82 is only 1-1.5 SD low. Within normal range or just below it.
- 3-SD fracture criteria (Eastell, McCloskey-Kanis): the cut-off is about 0.74, so this does not qualify.
- Only the old 15% Melton rule would call it a deformity.
- T9 is a little short overall: its back height is also about 8% below its neighbours'. That fits a developmental or growth-related cause better than a wedge compression fracture, which leaves the back height intact.
- The middle height through the node (14.9 mm, 0.73 of the back height) would set off an automated "biconcave fracture" flag. A small, corticated node is correctly excluded from fracture grading.
- Scheuermann's disease: only T8 (about 5-6°) and T9 are clearly wedged 5° or more; T7 is about 4.5-5°. That does not reliably meet the rule of three wedged vertebrae in a row, and the curve of the spine in this segment is not increased.

4) Other checks:
- Bone density is normal: 205-220 HU in T7-T11, with T9 no different from the others. That argues against a weak-bone fracture.
- There is no fracture line and no buckling of the front wall.
- The level is still presumed. Both segmentation models call it T9 and the rib heads line up consistently, but neither the first rib nor the T12/L1 junction is in the scanned range, so the count could be off by one level.

Bottom line: the category (benign-incidental) and severity 1 are right. Calling the wedging "borderline" is, if anything, cautious.

NOT REFUTED. The finding is real, the "benign-incidental, severity 1, no action" call is proportionate, and I'd keep it. One wording change: the wedging is a little worse than the reviewer stated. It straddles the 20% threshold rather than sitting below it, but that doesn't change what anyone should do.

1) The node is real. I confirmed it on my own renders in all three planes: native sag_st #95-#98, cor_st #96-#98, axial_st #19 (z=1740.25) and thin_lung 3-slice averages at z 1738.75-1743.25. It is a corticated, sclerotic-rimmed, tent-shaped central depression of the T9 inferior endplate. Apex is at about LPS (-15.5, -113.5, 1744); the opening runs from y -120 to -109 (about 11 mm AP, about 9 mm transverse) and it is about 5-6 mm deep. The content is 76 HU, which is disc-like. It does not look like infection, a tumor or a Cupid's-bow variant. Disc heights are preserved.

2) The fleck is real. It is a 2-3 mm dense density (about 660 HU on axial_st #18, z=1737.25) at the anterior lip of the node, about 4-5 mm behind the anterior cortex (y about -121). It projects about 1.5 mm into the disc. It is not a separated vertebral corner.

3) Nothing looks acute. The anterior cortex is smooth with a rounded corner, and there is no step-off, buckling or fracture line (high-zoom sag #93-#99). Bone density is normal: trabecular HU is 211 at T8, 194 at T9 and 227 at T10, so this is not a fragility fracture.

4) The level is reasonable. TotalSegmentator v1 and v2 both label this vertebra T9. Neither T1 nor T12/L1 is fully in the field of view, so a ±1-level uncertainty remains and "presumed T9" is the right wording.

5) Wedging. My corner-based heights (endplate cortex centres, 1.5 mm inset) give T9 Ha/Hp 0.76-0.78 and a wedge of 9-10°. With a 3 mm inset it is 0.80-0.82. T8 measures 0.88-0.93 and T10 0.91-1.03. T9's anterior height is also about 20% below the average of its neighbours' anterior heights. So it is mildly more wedged than the reviewer's 0.82-0.84 and 5.8°; the angle depends on method (line-fit versus corner-to-corner). Better wording: "borderline-to-mild (about 18-24%, at most Genant grade 1), chronic-appearing."

6) Would a radiologist report it? On a calcium-score CT, an experienced radiologist would often leave out a lone Schmorl's node. At most they would write one line, such as "chronic-appearing mild anterior wedging of T9 with Schmorl's node." The main value of recording it is so a future scan isn't misread as a new fracture. It needs no bone density scan (DXA) and no follow-up imaging. It is only worth raising with his doctor if he has persistent mid-back pain or a history of significant trauma.

systems.title: Technique, image quality & artifacts
systems.summary: This is a technically adequate low-dose, prospectively ECG-triggered calcium-score CT. It was acquired in 4 sequential table steps of about 33.75 mm each, joined at z≈1717.0, 1750.75 and 1784.5 mm (LPS). Blood-pool noise on the calcium series is about 16 HU in the mid-heart, rising to about 21-31 HU in the lowest step over the upper abdomen. I found no significant cardiac or respiratory motion, no stair-step misregistration between steps, no truncation and no metal. The dominant artifact is banding where the steps join: horizontal CT-number bands, largest just above the lowest join (z≈1719-1728). There the posterior LV and descending aorta read +15 to +40 HU too high, and the upper spleen pole just below the join reads about 20 HU high. Together with low-dose noise, these bands explain all 41 faint ≥130 HU 'calcium' specks the pipeline found: every one lies at z 1698-1707 or 1720-1727 and none lies above z 1728. Coverage is limited and slightly different from what the task assumed: the top of the scan is only about 7-8 mm above the carina, not about 3 cm. So the aortic arch, upper mediastinum, lung apices and thyroid are not imaged, and the bottom stops at about T12, missing the kidneys and adrenals. Effective dose is about 0.44-0.82 mSv, roughly 2-3 months of natural background.

checked.result: 8 series in DICOM LPS, patient feet-first supine (FFS), Siemens SOMATOM X.ceed, 120 kV, 0.25 s rotation, 64x0.6 mm collimation (38.4 mm). Calcium series: Sa36d kernel, 3 mm slices every 1.5 mm (overlapping), 158 mm heart-centred field of view (FOV), image type '120KVP_EQ'. axial_st/axial_lung: 3 mm, 391x288 mm. thin_lung/cr_vessel_suppress: 1.5 mm every 0.75 mm, 381 mm FOV. cor_st/sag_st: 4 mm slabs every 2 mm. axial_lung_mip: 10 mm slabs every 2 mm. All series register to each other in LPS.

Present, harmless. axial_st #45 and axial_lung #45 (z=1818.25) are entirely -1024 HU, as are axial_lung_mip #64 (z=1814.75) and the top 3 rows (~0.8 mm, z>1818.8) of cor_st and sag_st. The top ~3 mm of anatomy exists only in thin_lung, calcium and the reformats. Missing anatomy on these images is not a finding.

checked.item: Noise in homogeneous ROIs, every series (SD in HU)
checked.result: Calcium: ascending aorta 16.1, LV 15.8, descending aorta 19.2, paracardiac fat 17.1; liver, subcutaneous fat and outside air are outside its 158 mm FOV. axial_st: 18.1 / 18.6 / 21.5 / liver 35.3 / subcutaneous fat 24.5 / air 13-17. axial_lung: 127 / 125 / 162 / 237 / 187 / air 62-89. thin_lung and cr_vessel_suppress (identical in soft tissue): 248 / 240 / 292 / 417 / 310 / air 104-168. cor_st: 13.8 / 14.5 / 18.9 / 26.0 / 19.3. sag_st: 12.0 / 11.9 / 17.0 / 25.3 / 17.0. axial_lung_mip: maximum-intensity projection, so SD is not a valid noise metric. Air SD is underestimated because values clip at -1024 (6-11% of air pixels clipped in axial_st, about 50% in the lung kernels).

checked.item: Slice-by-slice noise on the calcium series
checked.result: Lowest step (z<1717, upper abdomen): descending-aorta SD median 30.8 HU, LV 21.1, liver 31.5. Steps 2-4: descending-aorta SD about 19-20, LV about 16-18, soft-tissue global noise level 15-17. The rise at slices 11-17 (z 1700-1708) reflects higher attenuation in the lowest step (liver, spleen and stomach in the beam), not a step join. The rise at slices 24-29 (z 1719-1727) is the bright band just above join 1 (LV SD 18-22 HU with the mean raised to 62-68 HU). Per-slice table: calcium_series_per_slice_noise_and_steps.csv.

checked.item: Location of the 4 table steps (z, LPS)
checked.result: Join 1 = 1717.0 ±1, join 2 = 1750.75 ±0.75, join 3 = 1784.5 ±1 mm. Step 1 = 1681.75-1717.0, step 2 = 1717.0-1750.75, step 3 = 1750.75-1784.5, step 4 = 1784.5-1819.75. Table feed is about 33.75 mm with about 4.6 mm overlap of the 38.4 mm beam. Evidence: noise minima on the calcium series at 1716-1718, 1750.75 and 1784.75-1785.25; a noise jump in thin_lung at 1750.75→1751.5; horizontal banding on sag_st/cor_st exactly at these levels; and consistency with the dose numbers (DLP/CTDIvol ≈ 15.4 cm ≈ 4 × 3.84 cm).

checked.item: Stair-step misregistration at the step joins (heart, diaphragm, vessels)
checked.result: None detected. Heart borders, diaphragm domes and lung vessels are continuous across all 3 joins on coronal and sagittal views. Phase correlation between neighbouring calcium slices across the joins gives 1.1-1.2, 0.6-0.7 and 0.7-0.8 mm, inside the range between neighbouring slices within a step (median 0.7, p90 1.2, max 1.6 mm).

checked.item: Mean-HU shifts between and within steps
checked.result: Present (see the first finding). Blood CT number varies from 40 to 78 HU along z: about 45-50 HU in steps 1-2 and about 55-60 HU in steps 3-4 (descending aorta). Bands: +15 to +40 HU just above join 1, +10 to +15 HU just above join 2, and stripes at join 3. Within step 1, the liver drifts from 70 to 55 HU and the spleen from 54 to 77 HU between z 1686 and 1707.

checked.item: Cardiac motion (heart rate 85 bpm, mean of 82-88; reconstructed at 76%; temporal resolution ~125 ms)
checked.result: No significant motion. Heart borders, aortic root and annulus, and the mid-RCA in the right atrioventricular groove (z 1734-1748) look sharp without doubling or 'seagull' artifacts; there is at most minimal blur on a few RCA slices. The LAD dots in the anterior interventricular groove (z 1734-1756) and the left atrioventricular groove fat are also sharp. Non-contrast images limit how well motion of the vessel lumen can be judged.
None. Both diaphragm domes are smooth across join 1 on coronal and sagittal views (thin_lung). Lung-base vessels are sharp. There is no offset of the liver or lung bases between steps.

checked.item: Beam hardening and streaks (spine, shoulders, ribs, sternum)
checked.result: Shoulders: horizontal photon-starvation streaks across the posterior chest wall and scapular muscles at z ≳1790 (axial_st soft-tissue noise ~29 HU in step 4 vs 17-20 in steps 2-3). Heart: directional (oblique/front-to-back) streaky noise texture in the blood pool in steps 1-2. Spine, ribs and sternum: no significant dark bands or streaks into the heart or aorta.

No metal in the body. The topogram shows the ECG electrode snaps outside the scan range: near the shoulders at z≈1860-1866 and at the right lower flank at z≈1656. Thin lead wires lie just outside the skin at x≈-205 and x≈+178 (z 1795-1818) and cause no streaks. Arms are raised (no humerus over the chest on the lateral topogram), so there are no arm artifacts.

No truncation artifact. Body width is about 380-385 mm at the upper chest, inside the 391 mm axial_st display FOV. The 381 mm thin_lung/cr_vessel_suppress FOV crops at most a few mm of lateral skin and subcutaneous tissue at z≳1757. The 158 mm calcium FOV contains the whole heart and pericardium with 12-33 mm margins.

No rings on narrow-window views of the heart and liver. Edge slices (bottom ~1.5-3 mm, top ~1.5 mm) are markedly noisier: axial_st #0 liver SD 55 HU; thin_lung #0 high-pass noise 566 vs ~400 nearby, and #182 at 419 vs ~320.

z 1819.75 (top slice centre 1819.0). The carina is at z≈1812 (one airway lumen at z≥1812.25, two at ≤1811.5), so the scan top is only about 7-8 mm above the carina, not about 3 cm. The ascending and descending aortas are separate on the top slice, so the aortic arch and the origins of its branches are NOT imaged. Also not imaged: upper paratracheal mediastinum, thymus region, thoracic inlet, thyroid and the lung apices (lung is still present at the topogram's top edge, z 1876, so at least 5.7 cm of the upper lungs, roughly 15-20% of lung volume, is missing).

z 1681.75, about T12 (vertebral numbering is approximate because counting landmarks are absent). Included: the top ~4.5 cm of the liver (dome at 1727.5), the upper spleen, the gastric fundus and upper stomach, and the splenic flexure. NOT included: most of the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, both kidneys (at most a sliver of the left upper pole at the very edge) and both adrenals. The posterior lung-base tips (costophrenic recesses) extend an estimated 3-10 mm below the scan (lung area on the bottom slice is ~700-950 mm² per side).

Complete. The pericardium spans z 1696.8-1798.0, giving 15 mm (inferior) and 22 mm (superior) margins inside the scan, and lies entirely within the calcium FOV. The coronary origins and aortic root are at z≈1770-1784 (step 3).

Meets standard Agatston requirements: 120 kV-equivalent, 3 mm slices, calcium kernel, prospective triggering in diastole. Slices overlap (1.5 mm increment); Agatston is defined on contiguous 3 mm slices, and the pipeline applied a 0.5 overlap correction. At mid-heart the 130 HU threshold sits about 5.2 SD above blood (47 HU, SD 16). In the band just above join 1 it sits only about 1.8 SD above the background (87 HU, SD 24).

checked.item: Radiologist's caliper (ascending aorta 36.1 mm, axial_st #33, z=1782.25)
checked.result: Technically valid. The slice lies in step 3, 2.25 mm below join 3. There is no misregistration there, and banding of ±20 HU does not move the aorta-fat edge (about 170 HU contrast). The ascending aorta runs nearly along z at this level (centroid drift ≤4 mm over z 1775-1805, tilt ≈5-8°), so an axial caliper overestimates the true short-axis diameter by <1%. Expected precision is about ±1-2 mm on 3 mm non-contrast images.

checked.item: Partial-volume and post-processing pseudo-lesions in the lung series
checked.result: Present (see the last finding): the apex of the right hemidiaphragm dome appears as a hazy oval at z 1725-1729, with a smaller one on the left at z≈1719. ClearRead vessel suppression leaves hilar 'flare' at z≈1780-1795 and unsuppressed vessels on the top slice. ClearRead's report of 0 nodules is consistent with these being suppression residues.

AP topogram at 100 kV and lateral at 140 kV. The scan range, step joins and landmarks are mapped in atlas_01. The topograms are acquired separately, so the diaphragm position may differ by about 1 cm from the CT.

CTDIvol 2.01 mGy (image header) / 2.12 mGy (dose report); size-specific dose estimate (SSDE) 2.87 mGy (water-equivalent diameter 27.4 cm); DLP 31.39 mGy·cm (= 4 steps × 3.84 cm × ~2.04 mGy). Effective dose: 0.44 mSv with the chest factor k=0.014, or 0.82 mSv with the cardiac factor k=0.026. That is about 54-99 days of US natural background (3 mSv/yr), about 22-41 single-view chest X-rays (0.02 mSv each), or about 11-27 one-way US coast-to-coast flights (0.03-0.04 mSv each). This is at or below the roughly 1 mSv usually quoted for calcium scans.

findings.title: Banding at the table-step joins, with false CT-number shifts (largest just above the lowest join)
findings.description: Horizontal bands appear exactly at the 3 joins between the 4 table steps: join 1 at z≈1717.0, join 2 at 1750.75 and join 3 at 1784.5 mm. They are sharply horizontal, cross different organs, and line up across axial, sagittal and coronal views, so they come from the reconstruction, not anatomy. The strongest band is in the lowest ~10 mm of step 2 (z≈1719-1728). A posterior LV ROI at (12,-181) reads 86-89 HU (SD 23-25) at z 1722-1725, against 44-48 HU (SD 16-17) at z 1740-1743 in the same step. Over the whole LV the mean is 62 vs 47 HU, and the descending aorta reads 68-78 vs 43-47 HU. The texture there is streaky. Just below join 1, inside step 1, the upper pole of the spleen reads 70-77 HU against 54-57 HU lower down, while the liver drifts from 70 to 55 HU. As a result, the liver-minus-spleen difference flips from +16 to −17 HU depending on z. Smaller bands sit above join 2 (+10-15 HU) and at join 3 (thin stripes in the descending aorta). The likely cause is cone-beam or partial-scan shading at the edges of each step; this is inferred, since no raw data are available. Across the whole scan, blood CT number ranges from 40 to 78 HU depending on z.
findings.plainEnglish: The scanner took the heart pictures in four quick 'slabs', each about 3.4 cm tall, and stitched them together. Where the slabs join, the images have faint bright and dark stripes. This is a camera artifact, not something in your body. The brightest stripe lies over the bottom of the heart and makes the numbers there read a little high. That is why the computer found some fake 'calcium' specks there and correctly threw them out.
findings.location: Joins at z 1717.0, 1750.75 and 1784.5 (LPS). Strongest band: posterior LV/inferior heart and descending aorta at z 1719-1728, plus the upper spleen pole at z 1702-1710
findings.recommendation: No action for the patient. Readers should not use absolute HU from z 1700-1730 (or near 1751-1757 and 1784.5) for densitometry such as estimating blood hematocrit, liver-spleen steatosis indices, or judging 'hyperdense' myocardium or aortic wall. A ≥130 HU speck in z 1719-1728 needs persistence across slices, a size of at least 1 mm² and a coronary location before it counts. Sensitivity for a tiny, faint calcification at the inferior heart (PDA, crux, distal RCA) is somewhat reduced in this band.
findings.measurements: Posterior LV ROI (6 mm): 89.0±24.5 HU at z 1722.25 and 86.0±22.8 at 1725.25, vs 48.0±16.3 at 1740.25 and 44.3±16.8 at 1743.25. Whole-LV mean 61.9 vs 47.2 HU. Descending aorta 67.7 vs 44.3 HU (calcium series), or 70.4 vs 42.5-47.0 (cor_st). Spleen 70-77 vs 54-57 HU; liver 55-58 vs 70-72 HU.

votes.note:
I could not refute this finding; independent checks confirm it. It is a real reconstruction artifact at the table-step joins, not pathology, and not something the conversion pipeline introduced.

1) Join positions. The DICOM AcquisitionNumber and AcquisitionTime labels cannot locate the joins: they are inconsistent between series and about 10 mm lower than the image evidence. The top label covers 42.75 mm, which a 38.4 mm detector cannot do in one rotation. I located the joins from the image data instead, using thin_lung adjacent-slice noise correlation. In static tissue it rises to 0.84-0.85 (baseline about 0.74); in the heart it drops to about 0.70. This happens at z ≈ 1716.0, 1750.4 and about 1785.0, matching the reviewer's 1717.0, 1750.75 and 1784.5 within about 1 mm.

2) Banding is visible in the scanner's own reformats as sharp horizontal stripes. At the same z they cross the LV, the RA and the descending aorta, with a thin dark line at about 1716-1717.

3) The CT-number shifts reproduce in calcium, axial_st and thin_lung. Within-slice controls rule out anatomy:
- LV 65-68 vs RV 45-47 HU at z 1723-1727, flipping to LV 41-42 vs RV 47-48 at z 1745-1749.
- Descending-aorta blood jumps from 45.8 to 61.3 HU between adjacent 0.75 mm slices exactly at the join (z 1717.00 to 1717.75), then peaks at 71.5.
- Smoothed difference maps show +20 to +35 HU in the posterior heart and -10 to -20 HU in the anterior heart. Blood cannot do that; it is shading.

4) Liver and spleen. The drift persists with masks eroded in z, which excludes through-plane partial volume. In the same slices the left paraspinal muscle rises while the right falls, a left-right shading gradient. Axial views show no focal splenic lesion; the splenic cross-section is uniformly brighter.

5) Not a pipeline or conversion artifact: rescale slope and intercept are constant on every slice (1 / -8192), and the bands appear in the scanner's sag_st and cor_st reformats.

6) Not an intramural hematoma: the aortic stripes are horizontal, span the full lumen and continue into adjacent structures. They are not crescentic.

Corrections and nuances:
- Join 1 is better placed at about 1716 (blend zone about 1714.5-1718). The HU maximum lies 2-12 mm above it.
- Noise is not generally higher in the band. Aortic SD is 20-22 HU in the band vs 19-21 just above, so the LV-ROI SD gap (23 vs 17) reflects local streak texture.
- The band mainly cuts calcium-score specificity rather than sensitivity. 28 of the pipeline's 41 candidates at or above 130 HU sit in z 1717.5-1727.5, including all 3 'review' candidates (z 1722.6-1724.2), and none sit above 1727.5. On calcium-window images those 3 show only streak texture, with no discrete focus. The other 13 sit at z 1697.5-1707.5 in the noisier inferior heart (aortic SD 23-31 HU), not in the band.
- The cone-beam / partial-scan mechanism is still an inference, but it fits the directional in-plane patterns.

The reader caveat stands: do not use absolute HU near the joins for liver-spleen steatosis indices, blood density, or calling something 'hyperdense'. There is no implication for the patient's health.

I could not refute this finding. Its join positions and HU numbers reproduce within about 1-2 HU, using my own ROIs, masks and planes and three different kernels (Sa36d, Br40d, Bl64d).

The join positions are confirmed by the DICOM headers. Three per-step tags change value at the same z: tube current (170 / 177 / 130 / 149 mA), CTDIvol (2.31 / 2.40 / 1.76 / 2.01 mGy) and the ECG phase in ImageComments (78% / 76% / 75% / 75%). In the thin series they switch at z 1716.25, 1750.75 and 1785.25; in the calcium series at 1717.75, 1752.25 and 1786.75. That fits a 34.5 mm table feed: 4 x 34.5 mm = the 138 mm image stack. The claimed joins (1717.0, 1750.75, 1784.5) are within about 1.5 mm of these. Two cautions: AcquisitionNumber and AcquisitionTime switch about 10 mm lower (1705.75-1707.25, 1740.25-1741.75, 1774.75-1776.25), so they should not be used to locate the joins. The steps were also acquired top-down, so the reviewer's "step 1" at the bottom was acquired last.

The images show the band itself. In the native sagittal and coronal reformats there is a sharp horizontal edge at about z 1716-1717. Above it, a bright band about 10 mm tall runs across the LV, RA and descending aorta. Below it the tissue is darker and noisier. Low-pass HU maps show the shading is uneven within each slice: at z 1719-1728 the posterior heart reads 80-100 HU and the anterior heart 35-50 HU. The RV is not raised, so this is not a uniform slab, and no blood pool should have a gradient like that. At 1731-1749 the heart is uniform at about 45 HU. On the axial images the texture is streaky and fan-shaped, as described.

Clinical framing: the "concern" is only a reading trap. There is no health implication, so severity 1 (worth knowing, no action) is right, and 0 is also defensible. The trap is that two wrong conclusions could be drawn from the HU numbers. Using the upper liver/spleen levels gives a liver-minus-spleen difference of -10 to -21, which would falsely suggest fatty liver. The band values (aorta 70-80, posterior LV about 90) could falsely suggest dense blood or a hyperdense wall.

Two corrections to the recommendation:
1. Its speck filter does not work in this band. Persistence, area of at least 1 mm² and coronary location would not reject these noise specks: area and persistence do not discriminate here, and only location does. In the calcium series, all 54 candidates meeting Agatston criteria (130 HU or more, 1 mm² or more) inside the pericardium lie at z 1698-1727, and there are none elsewhere. Their peaks are only 136-167 HU, none sits in epicardial fat (ring medians 25-101 HU), 36 of 54 persist on the adjacent overlapping slice, and 24 of 54 even persist 3 mm away. The useful discriminators are a soft-tissue (not fat) surround, a low peak, and position in the band.
2. The main effect is lower specificity (false-positive specks), not lower sensitivity. The positive offset would push a faint real calcification up, not hide it, although the streaks do reduce conspicuity.

One addition: step-to-step offsets of about 10-15 HU exist even away from the joins. The descending aorta reads about 44 HU mid-step 2 against about 55-68 mid-step 3. So all absolute HU on this exam carry roughly ±15 HU of z-dependent uncertainty, rising to +20-50 HU at z 1700-1730.

Minor wording point: the bright bands sit beside the joins (mainly on the upper side of joins 1 and 2) rather than exactly at them.

I could not refute this finding. I checked it myself and it holds.

**The bands are real and are an artifact.** On sag_st #76, #81 and #87 (x = 25.5, 15.5, 3.5) and cor_st #58 and #63 (y = −190.7, −180.7), viewed with only margin ticks and no overlay lines, a sharply horizontal bright band sits at z≈1718–1730. It crosses the RV, septum, LV, descending aorta and paraspinal muscle at the same height, so it ignores anatomy. A darker band lies just below it (z≈1708–1716), partly mixed with real inferior epicardial fat. On the axial calcium slices #24–30 the posterior LV shows a radial, streaky brightening, while #38 looks normal. Smaller stripes are present above join 2 (z≈1752–1757) and at join 3 (z≈1783–1786) in the aorta. No real disease would make a flat horizontal plane that also brightens skeletal muscle.

**The numbers reproduce.** If anything the effect is slightly larger than reported. The spleen and liver drift is also confirmed with 3D-eroded masks. The paraspinal muscles do not brighten at the spleen's level (z 1703–1713), so that shading is regional rather than a whole-slice offset. On smoothed views it is diffuse, with no focal lesion.

**The join positions are right to within about 1 mm.** I measured how well the fine-grain noise matches between adjacent thin_lung slices. Apart from the top and bottom edges of the scan, this measure is unusual only at z≈1715.9–1717.4, 1750.4–1751.9 and 1784.9. The calcium series shows a dip at 1715.5–1717. The 138 mm image range divides into 4 × 34.5 mm steps, which puts the joins at 1716.25, 1750.75 and 1785.25. One caveat: the DICOM header tags change at different heights (AcquisitionNumber at ≈1711/1745.5/1780, AcquisitionTime at ≈1708/1742.5/1777). Those tags do not mark where the data actually switch steps, so nobody should use them to move the joins.

**Clinical relevance.** This is not a finding about his body. An experienced radiologist would not list it for a healthy 37-year-old; at most there would be a one-line image-quality remark. There is nothing to tell his doctor and no reason to repeat the scan. I keep severity 1 only in the sense of "worth knowing so the bright stripe on the reformats, or a reading of about 90 HU, is not misread as something real". Severity 0 would be just as defensible for a formal report. The recommendation is proportionate: no action for the patient, and no densitometry inside the bands.

**One refinement to the speck rule.** Inside the band, persistence across slices and a size of at least 1 mm² do not separate noise from calcium. All 41 pipeline candidates lie at z 1698–1727, and 28 of them are in the band. Several appear on 2–4 overlapping slices, and one is up to 8.5 mm² (candidate #22 at (6.7, −165.7, 1722.6): 174 HU on calcium and 203 HU on axial_st). Overlapping 3 mm / 1.5 mm slices share data, so seeing a speck on neighbouring slices is not independent confirmation. The deciding test is a coronary course in epicardial fat, judged against the dozens of identical specks inside the blood pool at the same height.

**Effect on the calcium score.** The band and the dark strip below it overlie the crux and PDA level. That is a small residual uncertainty about a tiny inferior lesion; it does not overturn the total of 0.

**Steatosis.** Measured at slices well away from both step edges (z 1692–1698), the liver reads about 67–68 HU and the spleen about 57–61 HU, a difference of +7 to +11. That gives no sign of fatty liver. The −17 HU value at the spleen's upper pole comes from the artifact.

findings.title: Low-dose noise creates faint ≥130 HU 'pseudo-calcium' specks, confined to two z-zones
findings.description: All 41 candidates at or above the 130 HU / 1 mm² threshold from the pipeline are faint (peak 140-177 HU, none ≥200 HU). They lie only in two zones. Thirteen are at z 1698-1707 (cluster centre (8,-230,1702)): the inferior heart and liver-dome region in step 1, where blood and liver SD is about 25-35 HU. Twenty-eight are at z 1720-1727 (centre (10,-175,1723)): the posterior LV and inferior wall inside the band above join 1, where the background is raised to about 85-90 HU. None lies anywhere in z 1728-1819. The three candidates the pipeline marked 'review' (#22 at (6.7,-165.7,1722.6), #30 at (-2.1,-167.9,1723.0) and #32 at (-2.4,-176.6,1724.2)) all sit inside the band near the posterior interventricular groove and blend into the streaky noise texture. A threshold sweep shows how noise-limited the calcium series is: 943 blobs at a 100 HU threshold and 65 at 130 HU.
findings.plainEnglish: Because this scan uses a very low radiation dose, the images are slightly grainy. A few grains happen to be as bright as tiny calcium deposits. All of them were faint and sat in the two grainiest or stripiest zones, so they are expected noise rather than real calcium. The software rejected them, which is the expected behaviour.
findings.location: Inferior heart and liver dome (z 1698-1707) and posterior LV/inferior wall (z 1720-1727)
findings.recommendation: Calcium reviewers should treat specks confined to these zones as noise unless they persist across slices, are ≥1 mm² on non-overlapping 3 mm slices and follow a coronary course. This supports the pipeline's Agatston score of 0 outside the bands.
findings.measurements: 41 specks in total: 13 at z 1698-1707 and 28 at z 1720-1727; peak HU ≤177. The 130 HU threshold is about 5.2 SD above blood at mid-heart vs about 1.8 SD in the band.

findings.title: Higher noise in the lowest table step and very noisy edge slices
findings.description: Step 1 (z<1717, upper abdomen and diaphragm) is about 1.5-2 times noisier than steps 2-4. On the calcium series, the descending-aorta SD is 30.8 vs ~19-20 HU and the liver SD is 31-35 HU. On thin_lung, robust soft-tissue noise is 396 vs 268-322 HU. The first and last images of each series are much worse still: axial_st #0 (z 1683.25) has liver SD 55 HU with coarse streaks, and the first ~3 and last ~3 thin_lung images reach 1.4-2 times the noise of their neighbours. Noise also jumps about 10% at join 2 in the thin series (268→301 HU), consistent with step-specific tube-current or attenuation differences.
findings.plainEnglish: The very top and bottom slices, and the lowest part of the scan (upper belly), are grainier than the rest. That is normal for this kind of low-dose scan. It only means fine details there should not be over-read.
findings.location: z 1681.75-1717 (step 1); bottom slices z<1687 and top slice z≈1819
findings.recommendation: Do not interpret liver texture, small low-density areas or fine lung detail on the bottom 1-2 slices or the top slice.
findings.measurements: Liver SD 54.8 HU on axial_st #0 vs 35.6 on #3. Thin_lung high-pass noise: step 1 median 396, step 2 268, step 3 301, step 4 322; edge slices 566 (bottom) and 419 (top).

findings.title: Streaks from the low dose: across the shoulders and through the heart's blood pool
findings.description: Horizontal photon-starvation streaks cross the posterior chest wall and scapular muscles at the upper levels (z≳1790, step 4). They are caused by the long left-right X-ray path through the shoulders at low dose, and raise axial_st soft-tissue noise to about 29 HU. In steps 1-2, the blood pool of the heart has a directional, striated noise texture (oblique to front-to-back; structure-tensor coherence 0.25-0.40 vs 0.07-0.18 in steps 3-4). This texture can produce linear or curvilinear pseudo-structures inside the cavities.
findings.plainEnglish: Thin streaks run across the shoulder area and through the blood inside the heart on some slices. They come from the low-dose beam passing through the thickest parts of the body. They are not structures inside you.
findings.location: Posterior chest wall at z 1790-1819; LV/RV blood pool at z 1700-1750
findings.recommendation: Do not read linear densities in the inferior cardiac blood pool as valve, flap or thrombus pathology, or posterior chest-wall striations at the top levels as muscle abnormalities.
findings.measurements: axial_st soft-tissue global noise level: step 4 median 29.2 HU vs 17-20 HU in steps 2-3

findings.title: Pseudo-lesions in the lung series: partial volume of the diaphragm dome and ClearRead residues
findings.description: The apex of the right hemidiaphragm dome, with the liver beneath it, is cut tangentially at z 1725-1729. On 3 mm and 1.5 mm lung images it appears as a hazy oval of about 25×35 mm (mean about −430 HU, area up to 750 mm²). On the ClearRead vessel-suppressed series it looks like a well-defined nodule-like blob centred at (-100.5,-175.9,1727.5). A coronal view confirms it is the dome. A smaller left-dome equivalent sits at about (83,-169,1719). ClearRead suppression also leaves hazy hilar 'flare' next to both main bronchi (z≈1780-1795) and unsuppressed vessel fragments on the top slice at (-63,-141,1819) and (53,-141,1819). Thin_lung confirms these are vessels.
findings.plainEnglish: On the lung pictures, the very top of the dome-shaped diaphragm (with the liver under it) shows up as a hazy round smudge. On the special 'vessels-removed' lung pictures it can even look like a nodule. It is simply your normal diaphragm cut through at its highest point. The vessel-removal software also leaves harmless smudges near the lung roots and on the top slice.
findings.location: Right lower lung zone at the right dome apex (z 1725-1729); both hila (z 1780-1795); top slice (z 1819)
findings.recommendation: Lung reviewers should check any 'opacity' or 'nodule' near the domes, the hila or the top and bottom slices against coronal thin_lung images before calling it.
findings.measurements: Hazy area 501 mm² at z 1725.25 and 753 mm² at z 1728.25 (axial_lung), mean about −433 to −517 HU. The liver dome apex is at z 1727.5.

calcium.summary: DIY Agatston score 0 (volume 0 mm³, mass 0 mg). Of 41 candidate specks ≥130 HU inside the pericardium, none was coronary calcium: all were noise on top of a table-step shading artifact, confined to two z-bands (z 1698-1707 and 1720-1727). Nothing in or around the heart reaches 200 HU. Three independent reviewers (candidate review, blind sweep, cross-reconstruction physics) agreed unanimously; their estimated probability that the true score is 0 was 0.87, 0.94 and 0.90.

limitations: Limited coverage: the lung apices, aortic arch, upper mediastinum, thyroid, kidneys, adrenals and most of the abdomen were not imaged. A calcium-score scan is not a lung-cancer screening CT or a full chest CT.

No contrast: the inside of the heart, the heart valves, the coronary artery walls (including soft, non-calcified plaque), clots and the aortic root cannot be assessed. Calcium score 0 does not rule out soft plaque.
Very low dose: image noise limits detection of tiny or faint abnormalities (e.g. sub-4 mm nodules, faint ground glass, small liver lesions). The sharp lung-kernel images are especially noisy.
Step-and-shoot banding at the table-step joins (z ≈ 1717, 1751, 1785 mm) creates CT-number shifts and stair-step mimics. Several 'findings' were traced to it.
No clinical history, symptoms, labs or prior scans were available. Vertebra and rib numbering is presumed (no T1 or lumbar landmark in the scan).
Measurements from AI segmentation (chamber volumes, fat volumes) are estimates; hand-checked measurements are labelled.
This is an AI analysis for curiosity and education. It is not a diagnosis and does not replace the official radiologist report.
method: Eight AI 'specialist' reviewers (heart; aorta & great vessels; lung nodules; lung parenchyma, airways & pleura; mediastinum; bones; upper abdomen & chest wall; technique & artifacts) each read every relevant series with a radiologist's checklist and standard criteria (Fleischner 2017, Genant, Framingham reference values and others). They rendered and inspected 1,037 images, measured with their own code and recorded pertinent negatives. Every finding of note (7) then went to three independent skeptic agents with different lenses (artifact & anatomy; measurement & criteria; clinical relevance). Each skeptic re-rendered and re-measured from scratch and tried to refute the finding. Majority-refuted findings were dropped: two were ('old healed rib fractures' turned out to be a table-seam artifact; 'moderate visceral fat' was normal). Coronary calcium was adjudicated separately by three more independent reviewers. In total 32 AI agents made about 2,500 tool calls. An attending-style synthesis (this summary) reviewed the key evidence images directly.
disclaimer: Not a medical device. For curiosity and education only. The official radiologist report is what counts; talk to your doctor about anything here.
